venue.name: Aboriginal Journeys Wildlife and Adventure Tours
venue.description: Aboriginal Journeys is a family owned company running whale watching and marine wildlife tours out of Campbell River. Trips go out on a 27 foot covered boat with twin engines, an onboard washroom and heater, and an open viewing deck at the stern. The company runs one tour a day between April 15 and October 20 and keeps each trip to a maximum of 8 guests. The published minimum age is 5 years old.
venue.address: Discovery Harbour Marina (G dock), Campbell River, BC

facility_notes.rain_backup: You are safe from the elements in our covered and enclosed vessel
facility_notes.bus_parking: Paid parking is available in the parking area near our location (between C and G docks). The ticket booth is near the main gate at the south entrance to the Marina.

restrictions: No metal water bottles or large backpacks allowed
We keep our tours to a maximum of 8 persons
venue.seasonal_notes: Trips depart daily April 15 to October 20, and only one tour is run per day.

programs.name: 5 Hour Whale and Wildlife Watching Tour
programs.description: The longer of the two scheduled trips, leaving Campbell River and working the waters around Discovery Passage, Johnstone Strait and the Salish Sea. The company looks for orcas and humpback whales as well as dolphins, porpoises, seals, sea lions, eagles and black bears, and says nothing is guaranteed with wild animals. Lunch is included in the child price. Departure is normally 11 am, and a 10 percent fuel surcharge is added to every tour. Pick up and drop off at Quathiaski Cove on Quadra Island can be arranged for groups staying on Quadra.
programs.what_children_do: Spend about five hours on a small covered boat with a heated cabin, a washroom and an open deck at the back to stand and watch from. They scan the water for whales, dolphins, seals, sea lions and eagles, and eat the lunch that comes with the trip.
programs.our_note: Five hours afloat with no way to get off partway is a long stretch for a five or six year old, so think about the youngest child in the group. Cameras are welcome but tripods, metal water bottles and large backpacks are not, and water is provided. Ask about the fuel surcharge when you book, because it is added on top of the ticket price.
programs.practical_summary: There is a washroom and a heater on board and the cabin is covered, so rain is not a reason to stay home. Somewhere to eat on shore, wheelchair access and coach parking are not stated, and the boat takes eight guests in total, so any group has to be very small.
programs.extra_fees_note: There will be a 10% fuel surcharge on every tour including private tours.
programs.cancellation_note: We reserve the right to cancel or modify any tour due to any adverse weather forecasts or any unforeseen circumstances.

programs.name: 3.5 Hour Whale and Wildlife Watching Tour
programs.description: The shorter scheduled trip, on the same covered boat and looking for the same animals as the longer tour. Lunch is not mentioned for this one. Departure is normally 11 am, a 10 percent fuel surcharge is added, and prices are quoted before tax.
programs.what_children_do: Spend about three and a half hours on a small covered boat, sitting inside the heated cabin or standing on the open deck at the back, watching for whales, dolphins, seals, sea lions and eagles.
programs.our_note: This is the version to pick if you are unsure how long the children will last on the water. Bring food, because lunch is only mentioned on the longer tour. Metal water bottles, large backpacks and tripods are not allowed on board.
programs.practical_summary: A washroom and a heater on board and a covered cabin, so weather is not usually a reason to cancel. No word on lunch space, wheelchair access or coach parking, and the whole boat only holds eight guests.
programs.extra_fees_note: There will be a 10% fuel surcharge on every tour including private tours.
programs.cancellation_note: We reserve the right to cancel or modify any tour due to any adverse weather forecasts or any unforeseen circumstances.

programs.name: Private Tour
programs.description: The whole boat booked for one group rather than shared with other passengers. The published rate is $450 per hour with a minimum of four hours and a maximum of 8 guests, so the total depends on how long you go out for. The 10 percent fuel surcharge applies to private tours as well.
programs.what_children_do: Spend at least four hours on the boat with only their own group aboard, watching for whales and other marine animals from the heated cabin or the open deck at the back.
programs.our_note: This is the only option that gives a group the boat to itself, and four hours is the shortest booking allowed. Because it is priced by the hour, ask for the full total in writing before you commit. Eight guests is still the ceiling, so count your adults in.
programs.practical_summary: Same boat as the scheduled tours, with a washroom, a heater and a covered cabin. The total price, whether lunch is included and whether the departure time can be moved are all things to settle on the phone.
programs.extra_fees_note: There will be a 10% fuel surcharge on every tour including private tours.
programs.cancellation_note: We reserve the right to cancel or modify any tour due to any adverse weather forecasts or any unforeseen circumstances.
programs.evidence: We keep our tours to a maximum of 8 persons

An orca at the surface of blue green water, with a tall black dorsal fin and a misty blow drifting above it.
A whale tail raised clear of the water with sunlit spray pouring off it.

gaps: The site never mentions school, daycare or any other kind of group, so there is no group rate, no note on how many adults have to come, and no way to tell from the site whether a group booking is handled differently.
The daycare answer is set to no only because the site publishes a minimum age of 5 years. Nothing on the site refuses groups outright.
Prices are published per adult and per child aged 12 and under, before tax. No school, daycare or group rate is published.

The private tour is priced by the hour with a four hour minimum, so no total price for a group is published and the cost fields are left empty. The length of a private trip is chosen by the customer, so no fixed length is recorded either.

No street address is published for the departure point. The contact page prints a mailing address in bold as Not our office Location, and says the floating office is at the Discovery Harbour Marina, G dock. The marina is what we recorded.

The map on the contact page renders as a blank box in a browser, but the page markup carries a marker titled Aboriginal Journeys. The coordinates come from that marker, and they land on Discovery Harbour.
Whether there is anywhere to eat a packed lunch before or after the trip is not stated. Lunch is included on the five hour tour only.
Wheelchair access, stroller access and coach or bus parking are not addressed anywhere. The parking note on the contact page covers cars only.
There is no minimum booking notice published, only a recommendation to phone for same day or next day trips.
Grizzly bears are not mentioned anywhere on the site. Black bears are the only bears listed among the animals that may be seen, so do not sell this as a grizzly trip.
The homepage carries no Open Graph image, so the hero photo is the office picture from the contact page, which is the building a group actually walks up to.
